title: Austin: Tax Fights, Wage Hikes, and Signs
summary:
*   **Citizen Requests & Public Space:** The City Council heard petitions for wage increases for firemen and water/light plant workers. It also approved a new electric sign for a business on Congress Avenue, but with the stipulation that it could not extend over the public street.
*   **Extensive Property Tax Appeals:** The Council dedicated considerable time to resolving numerous appeals from citizens challenging their property tax valuations. While some land value assessments were upheld, several property owners successfully argued for reductions in the assessed value of their buildings or machinery.
*   **Policy on Tax Delinquency & Citizen Relief:** In a significant policy decision, the city allowed a property owner to repurchase lots the city had acquired due to over a decade of unpaid taxes, stating a preference against permanent city ownership of citizen property. Additionally, the Council remitted several impound fees and issued a refund for an impounded mule that had been sold.

Regular meeting of the City Council : Austin, Texas, December 26, 1912.

The Council was called to order by the Mayor : Roll called : Present Mayor Wooldridge,
Councilmen Bartholomew, Hart, Haynes & P well 5 Absent none.

The minutes of the last regular and subsequent recessed meetings were read and approved.

The Mayor laid before the Council a petition from Citizens asking that the wages of
Firemen and Coal Passers at the Water and Light Plant, be increased, which was read and
filed. To increase
Wages Engineers
Councilman Bartholomew presented a petition from the Engineers and Firemen at the Water
and Firemen at Light Plant asking an increase of wages, which was read and filed.
W & L Plant
The Mayor presented a petition from A E Hancock asking permission to erect an Electric
sign at his place of business at 909 Congress Avenue, which was read.
Mayor Wooldridge offered the following resolution :

A.E. Hancock
Sign
Be it resolved by the City Council of the City of Austin : That permit be and is hereby
granted to A E Hancock Company to install and maintain at its place of business, 909
Congress Avenue in this City , an electric light sign, above the awning. The general
description of this sign is that it is to be of a metal frame, approximately eight inches
through, twelve inches high and six feet in length.
In this metal frame work glass panels are to be placed, upon which are to be painted
appropriate signs, which signs are to be illuminated within by electric lights.
The permit hereby granted, is to be carried out under the Supervision of the Asst Supt of
the Water, Light and Power Department, and is granted, held and to be accepted as
revocable at any time in the pleasure of the City Council .
This permit is to be deemed a substitute for the petition heretofore made by said A E
Hancock Co, in which petition the sign hereby authorized to be placed was petitioned to be
extended beyond the curb and across a portion of the street, which privilege this
Council declines to grant.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Bartholomew, Hart, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.

Approved, A P Wooldridge, Mayor.

Reports of City Officers:

The Mayor laid before the Council the report of the City Sexton for the month of November
1912, which was read and ordered filed.
The Council then recessed subject to call.

. The Mayor laid before the Council the following resolution : Whereas, taxes on lots 9 &
10, in Block No 7, in the City of of Austin ,in Travis County, Texas, due the City of
Austin, are unpaid unpaid for the years 1895, 1897, 1899,1900, 1901, 1902, 1903, 1904,
1905, 1906, 1907,1908, 1909,1910 & 1911, besides interest, penalties and costs, and,
Whereas, judgement was obtained in the Dist Court of Travis County, Texas, on the 14th day
of May 1903, for the sum of $ 5661.10, besides and penalties for the years 1895,
1897,1898, 1899,1900 & 1901, besides Caves WB Frannolic cost of Court, and said lots were
ordered sold to pay said amounts, subject, however, to redemption by the owner thereof
within two years from from the date of such sale, and, Whereas, said lots were sold under
Judgement , on the 4th day of August 1903, to the City of Austin, for the sum of $616.64
as the amount of said taxes , interest, penalty & cost, and a deed deed executed to said
City for same bearing date 9th day of
September ,1903 , and,
Whereas, said lots not being redeemed within said two years as on 18th of March 1912, the
said City of Austin filed suit in the District Court of Travis County Texas, against
Sallie G Brush, and Wm B Brush her Husband, who claimed to be the owners of said lots
praying for title and possession of said lots and for damages and costs, etc., and by
decree of said Court rendered on the 2nd day of April, 1912, the title and possession of
said lots were divested out of the said Sallie G Brush and Wm B Brush and vested in the
said City of Austin, and, Whereas, the taxes now due on said lots at this date, together
with interest, penalties and costs amount to the sum of $ 2,044.46, and, Whereas, Mrs
Sallie K Brush, claiming to be the owner of said lots desires to pay said amount of $
2,044.46, and obtain a deed from the City of Austin of all the rights, title and interest
of said City of
Austin in said lots, and,
Whereas, said City of Austin does not desire to acquire property property owned by any of
its citizens, on account of their non-payment of taxes ,but desires all property in the
boundaries of of the City of Austin ,to pay the taxes assessed against the same.
Therefore, Be it resolved by the City Council of the City of Austin , Amount due, Opts.
Ch. in that upon payment by the said Mrs Sallie K Brush to the City Collector of the City
of Austin ,the sum of $ 2,044.46, besides taxes for the current year 19 12, on or before
Dec 31st ,1912, the Mayor of the the City of Austin ,be and he is hereby authorized and
directed to to execute to Mrs Sallie K Brush ,any and all instruments in writing necessary
and proper to vest in the said Mrs Sallie K Brush, all the rights ,title and interest of
the City of Austin ,in and to and to said lots 9& 10, in Block No 7.
Approved J B Ouldin Rector, City Attorney.
Approved A P Wooldridge, Mayor

protest & Grade

. The Mayor laid before the Council the following Communication : To his Honor the Mayor &
Gentlemen of The Council:

Gentlemen :

I have good reason to believe ,that the grade ,as established , west of my property at
corner of 8th & Lavacca,will result in damage to the property.
I have protested as strongly as I know howagainst the unjust grading ,and I write to say
that, if any damage, small or large,shall result from the work now being done,I will bring
suit against the City. Yours truly,
Mrs Mary H Mitchell.
The communication was received and ordered filed.

Geo. Johnson
